decisions.reason: After two years this non-maritime recruitment offer remains far from the firm’s core and shows no visible traction, so its option value now looks weaker than the cost and distraction relative to more strategic maritime opportunities.

This superyacht crew recruitment service is adjacent to the firm’s crewing capabilities and likely inexpensive to keep open, so management would preserve the option while learning more about demand in this niche.

The maritime education programme is highly related to the firm’s training network and has already built a six-institution partner network soon after launch, indicating promising early value with remaining upside.
Emissions monitoring and compliance services fit the firm’s maritime compliance strengths and already show concrete execution success, making further commitment justified.

The emissions compliance dashboard is strategically aligned with the firm’s digital and environmental direction and, being integrated into existing ship-management software, is a low-cost option worth retaining while adoption becomes clearer.

The emissions compliance cost simulation tool complements the compliance service bundle and existing software platform, so keeping it preserves upside in a growing regulatory market at limited incremental cost.
